previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-surgical malabsorption and hypoglycemia requiring continuous gastrostomy tube feeds presented with recurrent sharp pain at the G-tube site after running out of oxycodone, without fever, chills, nausea/vomiting, or tube feed intolerance. Exam showed a clean, intact tube site without erythema or induration, and labs/urinalysis were unremarkable. She was admitted overnight to the bariatric surgery service for symptom control, maintained NPO by mouth with continuous tube feeds, monitored closely without evidence of infection or bleeding, and her pain was managed with oral oxycodone with brief IV hydromorphone for breakthrough before transitioning back to oral-only therapy. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, ambulatory, tolerating her tube feeding regimen, and was discharged home with instructions to resume home continuous feeds (NutriHep 50 cc/hr), monitor blood sugars, continue home medications, use PRN pain medications safely, and follow up with her surgeon.

multiple recent admissions with the same complaint. CT scans 
performed in the past have revealed non-specific inflammation 
around the tube without collection. Her tube has been exchanged 
without relief. 

Ms. ___ reports increasing pain since running out of oxycodone 
at home. She said that with Tylenol alone, her pain was 
unbearable. She began taking Naproxen with good effect but 
stopped this when she was informed by Dr. ___ NSAIDS 
greatly increase the risk of marginal ulcers. She presents today 
due to the severity of the pain. There has been no change in the
appearance of her g-tube site. She continues to tolerate her 
tube feeds though she does report they irritate the site. She is 
having bowel movements and passing gas and is drinking water 
without nausea or vomiting.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the Emergency Department on ___ with pain at her G-tube site. Upon arrival to ED she was 
evaluated by the Bariatric Surgery team and admitted overnight 
for pain control.

Neuro: The patient was alert and oriented throughout 
hospitalization; pain was initially managed with oral oxycodone 
with intravenous dilaudid for breakthrough pain. The intravenous 
dilaudid was then discontinued in preparation for discharge 
home. 

CV: The patient remained stable from a cardiovascular 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored.

Pulmonary: The patient remained stable from a pulmonary 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Good pulmonary 
toilet, early ambulation and incentive spirometry were 
encouraged throughout hospitalization. 

GI/GU/FEN: The patient continued on her home regimen of 
continuous tube feeds. Patient's intake and output were closely 
monitored during this admission.

ID: The patient's fever curves were closely watched for signs of 
infection, of which there were none.

HEME: The patient's blood counts were closely watched for signs 
of bleeding, of which there were none.

Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin and 
venodyne boots were used during this stay. She was encouraged to 
get up and ambulate as early as possible.

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
and hemodynamically stable. The patient was tolerating a diet, 
ambulating, voiding without assistance, and pain was manageable. 
The patient received discharge teaching and follow-up 
instructions with understanding verbalized and agreement with 
the discharge plan. She will follow up with Dr. ___ on 
___.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ with 
pain at your G-tube site. You were given Oxycodone with good 
effect. Please resume your home continuous tube feeds (NutriHep 
@ 45 cc/hour). Continue to monitor your blood sugars when you 
return home.

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:

*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.

*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.

*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.

*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.

*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.

*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.

*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.

*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.

*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids.

Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking pain 
medications.

Please follow up with your surgeon Dr. ___ at the 
appointment listed below.

Best wishes,
Your ___ surgical team
